transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Can you start by telling me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Yeah, um… I guess the main thing is I’m having a hard time actually staying with work I’m supposed to be doing. Like, I’ll sit down with a stack of essays to mark, or some curriculum document, and I really do mean to get through it.

But then ten minutes later I sort of… come to, and I’m still on the same page. I’ve been thinking about three other things—sometimes completely unrelated—and I haven’t really taken in what I was reading. It’s frustrating, because I’m physically there, I’ve got the work in front of me, but my mind just doesn’t stay on it.
Would you say this kind of difficulty focusing has been part of how your mind has always worked, even back in school, or is this something new that's started more recently?

Yeah, no, it’s definitely not new. I mean, I was thinking about that because my mum kept a bunch of my old school reports—she keeps everything, honestly, like even birthday cards from people I barely remember—but yeah, even in primary school they’d say things like I was bright but careless.

There were comments about not finishing work unless the teacher was basically right there watching me. And my parents were always finding worksheets all crumpled up in the bottom of my backpack that I’d just forgotten to hand in. I remember getting in trouble for that and being like, “I did it, though,” but obviously that didn’t help if no one ever saw it.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or noticing that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in things you’d normally enjoy?

Um… I don’t think so? Not in a way I’ve really clocked. I mean, everyone has off days, right—especially at school, when the timetable gets weird or there’s some assembly that throws everything out, and then the whole day feels sort of… scrambled.

But sad, like properly down for days, or not enjoying things at all—I haven’t really noticed that. I still like the things I usually like when I actually get to them. I guess I haven’t been tracking it very closely, though.

Do you notice yourself feeling restless, fidgety, or having trouble sitting still for long periods—like in meetings or while watching a movie—or acting impulsively, such as blurting things out or making quick decisions without thinking them through?

Um… I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, I fidget sometimes, I suppose, but I don’t know if it’s more than anyone else. Meetings are hard, but part of that is just because school meetings can go on forever about, like, the wording of one policy paragraph, and then someone brings up photocopying budgets and suddenly it’s twenty minutes later.

But no, I don’t think of myself as someone who’s constantly needing to move around or blurting things out all the time. Quick decisions… maybe with small things, like buying some random teaching resource online and then realizing I didn’t really need it, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean. I haven’t really noticed that as the main problem.
Does this same kind of difficulty focusing or following through happen in other parts of your life too—like at home, managing bills or chores, or in personal relationships—not just at work?

Yeah… it’s not just work, unfortunately. I wish it were, because then I could sort of blame the school systems, you know? There are so many little forms and emails and half the platforms don’t talk to each other properly—anyway.

But no, it happens at home too. My wife has kind of… started taking over bills and reminders and things like that, because she can’t really rely on me to keep track of them. Which feels awful to say, because I’m a grown man and I can manage a classroom, but then I’ll miss some basic life admin thing unless she’s chasing it.

And at work it’s got serious enough that my department chair put me on a support plan, mainly because of missed follow-through. Like not finishing or not following up on things I said I’d do. So… yeah, it’s definitely across more than one part of my life.
Have you noticed yourself feeling unusually worried, tense, or on edge much of the time recently, in a way that might be distracting you from tasks?

I don’t think so? I mean, I worry about normal stuff—work, whether I’ve forgotten something, whether I’ve replied to the right parent email or left a form sitting in some online portal. There are so many portals now, honestly, it’s ridiculous—one for attendance, one for safeguarding, one for behaviour, and none of them seem designed by anyone who’s ever worked in a school.

But, sorry, your question was whether I feel worried or tense most of the time. I wouldn’t say that’s the main thing. I don’t feel constantly on edge, exactly. It’s more like I suddenly realize I’ve missed something and then I get stressed about that. I’m not sure if that counts.
How has your sleep been lately—are you getting enough good-quality sleep most nights, and do you use alcohol, cannabis, or other recreational substances regularly?

Um… sleep. I’m not totally sure how to judge “good-quality,” honestly. I mean, I go to bed, and then sometimes I’m lying there thinking about whether I’ve set my alarm or whether I need to prep something for the morning, but I don’t know if that’s unusual or just… being an adult with a job.

Some weeks are better than others, I suppose. And substances—no, I mean, I’m not really someone who’s… actually, what counts as regularly? Like a drink at a staff thing or if we’re out for dinner? I wouldn’t say I’m using anything in a way that feels like a big part of my life. Cannabis, no, not really my thing. Other stuff, no. But yeah, with sleep, I’d have to think about it more because I don’t really track it or anything.
Do you often lose or misplace things you need, like your keys, phone, wallet, or important paperwork?

Yeah, all the time. I’m constantly hunting for things I need for the day—classroom keys, lesson notes, my USB drive, that sort of thing.

It’s silly because I’ll be absolutely sure I had them in my hand five minutes earlier, and then suddenly they’re just… gone. And if I’m refereeing, it’ll be the whistle or the cards, which is not exactly ideal when you’re supposed to look organised. Then I end up checking the same bag pockets three times, even though obviously if it wasn’t there the first time—well, sometimes it is there the third time, somehow.
Can you tell me about a specific time when this difficulty with focus or follow-through caused a real problem—like at work, with money, or in your relationship—and how serious the consequences were?

Yeah… I mean, work is probably the clearest example. It’s not just “oh, I forgot a photocopy” kind of thing anymore. I’ve missed follow-through on enough things—forms, emails, bits of planning or admin—that my department chair has actually put me on a support plan.

Which sounds very official, and it is, I suppose. It was a bit humiliating, honestly, because I do care about the job. I’ll start something with every intention of finishing it, and then something else comes in—someone knocks on the classroom door, or there’s a behaviour issue, or I open the wrong tab and suddenly I’m dealing with three other things. Schools are basically designed to interrupt you every seven seconds, but still, other people seem to manage it better than I do.

At home it’s caused problems too. My wife has started taking over the bills and reminders, not because she wants to be in charge of everything, but because she can’t really count on me to keep track of them. That’s been… not great. It makes me feel like a child sometimes, and I know it frustrates her. So yeah, I’d say the consequences have become pretty serious.
